{{Quote|Coruscant's humans may have come into dominance on their homeworld by defeating a near-human species known as the Taungs in several series of legendary battles.|[[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]], hypothesizing the possible origins of humans|<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>}}
A '''war''' took place on [[Coruscant/Legends|Notron]], the homeworld of both the [[Taung/Legends|Taung]] and the [[Zhell/Legends|Zhell]] species. It was famously recorded in the ancient epic poem ''[[Dha Werda Verda]]''.

==Prelude==
Thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the rise of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Notron]] was inhabited by two [[Species/Legends|species]]: the [[Taung/Legends|Taungs]] and the [[Zhell/Legends|Zhell]].<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> The Zhell organized themselves into the thirteen [[Battalions of Zhell]],<ref name="Warfare" /> also known as the Nations of Zhell,<ref name="Atlas" /> and eventually came into conflict with their Taung neighbors.<ref name="Warfare" /> The Zhell were theorized among academics to be the ancient ancestors of the modern [[Human/Legends|humans]], but this was hypothesized and remained unproven.<ref name="Galaxy" />

==The war==
According to the account of ''Dha Werda Verda'', the two armies skirmished for centuries. Eventually, the Taungs led by a [[General/Legends|General]] nicknamed the [[Doom of Ulmarah]] successfully took [[Great Zhell]], the Zhell capital, but with heavy losses, the Doom among them. The Zhell besieged the city and the Taungs, now led by [[Rexutu the Unconquerable]], resolved to make their last stand there.<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Author's Cut 2" />

With the Taung defeat apparently imminent, a [[Volcano/Legends|volcanic eruption]] brought devastation upon the Battalions of Zhell, which it smothered their army with thick ash and nearly destroyed their race. The enormous plume of ash and smoke was so dense and widespread across the sky that it blocked out the light from the sun, leaving the land beneath in darkness for two years. The Taungs immediately took the advantage that nature had provided, and in the aftermath of the eruption, subjugated their age-old enemy.

The Taungs viewed the smoke and shadow as an emblem of their destiny, and it was then that they adopted the name ''[[Dha Werda Verda]]'' for themselves, a title that meant "Warriors of the Shadow" in the [[Mando'a/Legends|Taung language]]. However, the Taungs' victory over the Zhell was doomed to be a fleeting one. Over time, the Zhell eventually managed to win back control of Notron and drive the Taungs from their shared homeworld.

==Aftermath==
The defeated Taungs fled to [[Roon/Legends|Roon]], where they left behind a number of artifacts that were found by future [[Archaeologist/Legends|archaeologists]], as well as the text of ''Dha Werda Verda'' written in [[Roonstone]]s. The Taungs then began a nomadic existence, roaming through the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] until they settled [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]], becoming the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]].<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Author's Cut 2" />

Disagreement raged among academics as to the historicity of ''Dha Werda Verda's'' account. [[Arhul Manaxa]] of the [[University of Rudrig/Legends|University of Rudrig]] noted in [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]] that no known species, not even the [[Columi/Legends|Columi]], possessed [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] travel two hundred thousand years before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], and so questioned how the Taungs could have fled Coruscant to a planet on the other side of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. He speculated that the war may have taken place later than the traditional dates suggested while the galaxy's eldest species were exploring the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. Additionally, ''Dha Werda Verda'', and historical re-enactments, depicted the Taungs and Zhell as using [[Sword/Legends|swords]], [[Spear/Legends|spears]] and [[Axe/Legends|axes]], of the sorts found in Taung burial sites on Roon. However, military historian [[Hu Jibwe]] of [[Salmagodro Grand Academy]] noted that these finds from Roon were ceremonial weapons, and pointed out that no [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]]-capable society still used such [[Melee weapon/Legends|melee weapons]], even suggesting that the poem may have been the corruption of a battle fought by much more advanced parties equipped with aircraft and [[Nuclear weapon/Legends|nuclear weapons]].<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Author's Cut 2" />
